aboutMe.intro: I'm Keishmer Pérez Torres, a Product Designer and Frontend Developer who helps startups, service companies, and premium brands turn an unclear digital presence into experiences that feel credible, strategic, and ready to grow. My work combines UX/UI, brand systems, and frontend execution so clients can move faster without splitting strategy, design, and implementation across multiple freelancers.
aboutMe.professionalSummary: Keishmer Pérez Torres is a Product Designer and Visual Artist with over 4 years of experience across digital product design, university teaching, and multimedia production. He holds a Master's degree in Multimedia Design and Production from Universidad Internacional de la Rioja (Spain) and a Bachelor's in Visual Arts from Universidad de Pamplona (Colombia). He currently works as a Product Designer at Move On Tech Service, leading visual and functional design for digital solutions in the security and logistics sector. Previously, he served as a university lecturer in Industrial Design, coordinated digital library services, and created multimedia content for educational and cultural institutions. With 40+ certifications in design, development, AI, SEO, and marketing, he brings a multidisciplinary approach to every project — combining artistic sensibility, technical precision, and strategic thinking to deliver solutions that create real value for people and brands.
aboutMe.exp1Desc: Leads visual and functional design of digital solutions focused on security and high-value logistics. Develops interactive prototypes in Figma to optimize user experience across mobile, web, and multi-device platforms. Maintains a hands-on approach to product design, UX research, and front-end collaboration.
aboutMe.exp2Desc: Led research and product creation processes using user-centered design methodologies for wood products, technical drawing, and manual illustration. Taught courses on two-dimensional and three-dimensional representation with physical materials and guided practical workshops on contemporary design trends and fundamentals.
aboutMe.exp3Desc: Led the transition and management of library services to digital environments. Implemented academic search tools, open access resources, and content curation strategies. Established visual communication campaigns to promote scientific databases and research resources across the university community.
aboutMe.exp4Desc: Created graphics, videos, and interactive content for educational and cultural campaigns. Supported institutional communication through visual design and multimedia tools. Optimized the brand's omnichannel experience across digital and physical touchpoints.

faq.title: Common project questions
faq.oneQuestion: What type of projects are a good fit?
faq.oneAnswer: The best fit is a startup, service company, or brand that needs UX/UI, frontend development, branding, or a connected combination of those services.
faq.twoAnswer: Projects under US$1,000 can be considered depending on scope. The form asks for a range so I can recommend the most realistic next step.
faq.threeQuestion: Do you work remotely and in both languages?
faq.threeAnswer: Yes. I work remotely with clients worldwide in English and Spanish.
faq.fourAnswer: I usually reply within 24 hours with a short follow-up or the next question needed to assess the project.
faq.fiveQuestion: What do you need from me to start?
faq.fiveAnswer: A clear description of the problem, any existing brand or product materials, and access to stakeholders who can give feedback. The more context you share, the faster I can propose the right direction.
faq.sixQuestion: How long does a typical project take?
faq.sixAnswer: A focused landing page or brand identity can take 2–4 weeks. A complete website or product interface typically ranges from 4–8 weeks depending on scope and revisions.
faq.sevenAnswer: You receive the source files, design system, responsive prototypes, and a maintainable frontend build with documentation for next steps.
faq.eightQuestion: Do you work with existing teams or developers?
faq.eightAnswer: Yes. I can plug into existing product, marketing, or development teams and handle the design layer while your team focuses on engineering, content, or operations.

brand.title: Design system & brand manual
brand.lede: The single source of truth for how this site looks and reads. Every value here is generated from the tokens the site actually ships, so this page stays in sync with production.
brand.metaLine: One dark theme · EN/ES · Astro + Tailwind v4 + GSAP

howToRead.title: How to read the swatches
howToRead.body: Each swatch shows the token name, its hex value, and its contrast ratio against the page background. Click any swatch to copy the hex. AA needs 4.5:1 for text; 3:1 is only acceptable for large text and decorative elements.

logo.title: Logo & brandmark
logo.intro: The public mark is the KEISHMER STUDIO wordmark — Unbounded for display, VT323 Mono for the nav — plus the K monogram, the letter K in Unbounded, for tight spaces and the favicon.
logo.clearSpaceBody: Keep at least the cap height of the wordmark clear on every side. Nothing crowds the mark.
logo.minSizeBody: 18px tall for the monogram, 140px wide for the full wordmark. Below that, use the monogram alone.
donts: Stretch, rotate, or recolor the mark
Set it on a low-contrast background
Add shadows, outlines, or gradients to it

color.title: Color
color.intro: A single dark theme built on near-black surfaces, a light icy-gray text ramp, and one coral accent. Color is classified by role, not by hue.

brand.title: Brand & accent
brand.desc: The coral primary is the single accent. Blue appears only inside the call-to-action glow; pink is a soft tint reserved for highlights.

surface.title: Surfaces
surface.desc: Near-black neutrals. The page always paints black; panels lift with slightly lighter grays.

text.title: Text
text.desc: A light ramp for dark surfaces. text-white is the default body voice; white is for icons and the wordmark.

neutral.title: Neutral grays
neutral.desc: The working scale for borders, muted text, dividers, and secondary surfaces.

state.title: State
state.desc: Feedback for forms and system messages. Never the only signal — always paired with text.

notes.primary: The only accent. One per view.
notes.primaryInverse: Deeper coral for strong hover / pressed states.
notes.accentBlue: Used only in the CTA glow animation.

typography.title: Typography
typography.intro: Three voices: Unbounded for display, Albert Sans for body, and VT323 Mono for labels and the wordmark. Size and weight are independent axes.

familyNotes.mono: Labels. Buttons, breadcrumbs, eyebrows, the wordmark — always uppercase with wide tracking.

typography.uppercaseNote: Mono labels are set uppercase with tracking-widest. Display headlines are uppercase in Unbounded bold.

spacing.title: Spacing
spacing.intro: A 4px base scale from Tailwind. Component padding lives between 8 and 32px; section rhythm is larger and consistent.
spacing.rhythmBody: Horizontal padding steps up with the viewport: px-4 → md:px-8 → lg:px-24. Vertical sections open with py-16 → lg:py-20. Content is capped at max-w-6xl.

radius.title: Radius & stroke
radius.intro: Mostly sharp edges. Radius is reserved for chips and pills; borders are thin hairlines.
radius.note: Borders lean on opacity (border-white/10 → /40) instead of new colors. Hairline is the default for dividers and cards.

elevation.title: Elevation & shadow
elevation.intro: Depth is built with surfaces first and shadows second. The only branded shadow is the coral glow on the primary CTA hover.

notes.flat: Flat by default — surfaces and borders carry hierarchy.
notes.glow: hover:shadow-lg shadow-primary/50 — the coral glow, reserved for the primary action.
notes.drop: drop-shadow on logos over imagery for legibility.

motion.title: Motion
motion.intro: GSAP drives entrances, scroll-scrub, and the featured-projects pin. Everything collapses to no motion under prefers-reduced-motion.
motion.reducedNote: With prefers-reduced-motion, animations are skipped and content is shown in its final state.

easingNotes.power3InOut: Large panels and the menu overlay.

layout.title: Layout & breakpoints
layout.intro: Tailwind's canonical five breakpoints. Content is centered and capped; the featured-projects rail scrolls horizontally below lg.
layout.containerNote: Sections use mx-auto max-w-6xl as the main measure. The featured carousel swaps to a horizontal scroll-snap rail under lg.

iconography.title: Iconography
iconography.intro: Inline SVG in the Material Symbols style, always filled with currentColor so icons inherit the color of the text they accompany.
iconography.note: Sizes pair with the type scale: 20px inside buttons, 24px in navigation and lists. Decorative icons are aria-hidden; informative icons carry a label.

effects.title: Effects
effects.intro: The quiet layer: gradients, the marquee, and generative canvas backgrounds.
effects.gradientsBody: Tailwind v4 linear and radial gradients (bg-linear-to-*, bg-radial). Used to fade edges and to sit type over imagery.
effects.marqueeBody: An infinite scroll of services (ServiceBanner). Pauses on hover and disables under prefers-reduced-motion.
effects.canvasBody: BlackHoleBG, CursorParticles, and MeshText render generative visuals. They are decorative and always sit behind content.

components.title: Components
components.intro: The live building blocks, rendered with the same classes the site ships.
